_doc: Release Manifest precursor. Describes WHAT is being released so the gate checks a committed declaration rather than whatever flags an operator typed. commitSha/buildId/deploymentId are left null until a release is cut - the gate fills the comparison from the build itself, and only enforces a field that is set here. This is NOT the Change Registry: no change IDs, no Firestore, no UI.

_changeNotes.FIX-0042: Connection-aware Master Data import. In production 3.21.4 stopped at 11,036 / 30,166 (11,001 written, 35 outcome unknown): a silent network stall timed out group after group of 4 records at 90 s each until the 25-failure guard ended the run. Now, after any group in which a record timed out, the loop asks the backend itself with a bounded read-only probe (probeMasterDataBackend: one document from the server, never the cache, nothing written; 15 s). If the backend does not answer, the run PAUSES in CONNECTION LOST - no new record starts, the timeouts do not consume the failure guard, and the probe repeats every 10 s until the server answers (resume with the next record), the user stops (INTERRUPTED) or 30 minutes pass (INTERRUPTED, resumable). A timed-out record stays OUTCOME UNKNOWN and is never retried in the run. If the backend answers while writes keep timing out, those timeouts count toward the guard (a slow server); confirmed failures count exactly as before. createMasterDataItem / updateMasterDataItem report each awaited step (duplicate lookup, Firestore write, cache cleanup, audit write - none removed or reordered), so every timeout records the step it waited for, its start and timeout times, the page visibility, the browser online signal, and the source file and row. The heartbeat shows the connection state, paused time, last server answer, last successful write and the current operation. Batch size 250 and concurrency 4 unchanged. No business rule, validation, audit, cache behaviour, Firestore rule, schema or permission changed; nothing was imported
_changeNotes.FIX-0041: Master Data import hang (3.21.3 stopped at 21% = 6,500 / 30,166 for 30 minutes in batch 6,501-6,750). Each record write waits on a duplicate lookup, the Firestore write, a local-cache cleanup and an audit write, and none of those waits was bounded: a Firestore write stays pending while the connection is lost or the machine sleeps, and an aborted IndexedDB transaction left the cache promise pending forever (no onabort). A pending promise is not a failure, so the consecutive-failure guard never fired, and the stop only acted between batches. Fix (entityImportExecutionPure): every record is bounded by IMPORT_RECORD_TIMEOUT_MS (90 s); past it the row is recorded as OUTCOME UNKNOWN - the server may or may not have committed it - separately from confirmed failures, counted toward the failure guard, never retried in the same run, and a BOM depending on it says so. A stop is a real AbortSignal: no new write or batch starts after it, and writes already in flight get STOP_GRACE_MS (5 s) before they are recorded as outcome unknown. Progress is reported every second between batches with the time of the last outcome. localCacheStore: every IndexedDB operation settles on success, error, ABORT, exception or CACHE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS (10 s), falling back as before. The screen shows the last progress time, a "waiting for the server" warning after 60 s without progress, the browser online/offline signal (informational only), the stop state, and outcome-unknown counts and records; 100% still means every phase ran and the verification passed, and a run with an unknown outcome is never reported as a success. A re-run matches committed records by identity and never duplicates them. No business rule, validation rule, audit, cache, Firestore rule, schema or permission changed; nothing was imported
_changeNotes.FIX-0040: Master Data Package final re-check fix (3.21.2 wrote 222 of 30,166 rows). Two defects in the final pre-write re-check, which - unlike the preview - resolved business codes against the Firestore reference indexes: (1) each product row's OWN productCode was looked up as a reference to another product, so every new product was rejected ("No record matches", or "suggestions must be approved manually" for close codes), and every BOM depending on it was then dropped; (2) the BOM row's top-level `version` object matched the `version` alias of bomVersionCode and was looked up as an existing BOM version. Fix: resolveAndValidateImportRow runs no business-code resolution for the self-identified package kinds (products, materials, bomPackage) - their identity and resolved ids / pending tokens are already on the row - so the preview and the final re-check now run identical rules; and readReferenceValue reads only scalar values, so an object under an alias name is never taken as a code (a real version code is still read). Resolution is unchanged for every other kind. The summary strip is relabelled as totals of all runs in the window, the final panel as this run's result; a finished or stopped import shows its closing message and a "Close window" button and never closes by itself. Replayed on the real package with real indexes and a recording writer: 15,872 products + 221 materials + 14,073 BOMs written, 0 not written, 0 failed; the 29 blocked BOMs and 85 skipped duplicates unchanged; a re-run over the state 3.21.2 left updates its 221 materials and 1 product and creates nothing twice. No business rule, validation rule, Firestore rule, schema or permission changed; nothing was imported
_changeNotes.FIX-0039: Large Master Data Package import: live progress, batches and a verified final result. The ~30,000-row import previously ran as one uninterrupted await chain with no feedback, and the review table rendered every row (with its payload serialised twice) on every change - enough to leave the browser white. The execution loop (entityImportExecutionPure) now runs in three dependency phases (Products & Materials -> Resolving Dependencies -> BOMs) in batches of 250, reports a progress snapshot and yields to the browser after each batch, writes up to 4 package rows at once (every other import stays strictly one at a time), stops between batches on request or after 25 consecutive failed writes, never throws, and returns its own verified final result (counts by kind, failures and dropped rows with reasons, phases completed, verification). The percentage is floor(processed / total), clamped, and 100 only after every phase ran and the verification passed. The screen shows READY / IMPORTING / VERIFYING / COMPLETED / COMPLETED WITH ERRORS / INTERRUPTED from those numbers only, locks the rows while running, guards against leaving the page, keeps a counts-only checkpoint of an interrupted run, and pages the review table (100 rows, filterable). Resuming is re-running the same package: existing records are matched and updated, never duplicated. No business rule, validation rule, Firestore rule, schema or permission changed; nothing was imported
_changeNotes.FIX-0038: Master Data Package import dependency fix (3.21.0 defect). A BOM whose product or components are created by the SAME package carried a blank item id: the preview showed it ready and the final pre-write validation dropped it ("rows excluded before write"). Now a package-created item is referenced by a pending package-item token (never an id, never written); the preview validates every BOM with the SAME validator the write uses, over the existing items plus the package items, and a BOM whose package item will not be written (blocked, skipped, excluded or warnings not accepted) is BLOCKING with that reason. The single approved import writes products and materials first, binds each token to the ASFOUR id its write returned, then revalidates and writes the BOM (entityImportExecutionPure). Also fixed on the same path: the Odoo BOM id external reference was dropped by normalisation; an existing BOM and its V1 were flagged as duplicates of themselves on re-import; unchanged records are no longer rewritten (NO-OP); lookups are indexed (the real package preview/execution went from over 10 minutes to seconds); re-selecting the same files re-reads them. Real package: 15,872 products + 221 materials + 14,073 BOMs importable in one run, 0 dropped before write; 29 BOMs stay BLOCKING by the unchanged BOM rules (24 with a line quantity <= 0, 5 with an item listed twice) and never block the others. No business rule, BOM validation rule, Firestore rule, schema or permission changed; nothing was imported
_changeNotes.UI-0037: Translation governance and print styling. A Translation Manager and a Language Audit screen (gated by the new translation.manage permission) read and write translationOverrides, whose rule already exists; LanguageContext merges the overrides for signed-in users. The header, sidebar, mobile navigation and footer are hidden when printing. No production, Master Data or costing behaviour changed
_changeNotes.AI-0036: AI Assistant through the assistant gateway. The AI Assistant screen now drives the same AssistantGateway / tool registry / permission checks as the Global Assistant, and the old client-side aiService was removed. A real provider is reached only through the separately deployed Cloudflare Worker in cloudflare/ai-gateway (NOT deployed by this release); VITE_AI_PROVIDER defaults to the local mock, so nothing calls an external model until that gateway is configured. Suggested Analytics is reachable from the sidebar. No API key is shipped in the bundle
_changeNotes.SEC-0035: Backup integrity before restore. The previous restore preview treated every checksum as valid (a trailing "|| true"). Restores now verify the file fingerprint (SHA-256, or the legacy CHK- checksum for older backups) and STOP on a mismatch; a backup with no checksum needs an explicit allowance. Collection counts use getCountFromServer instead of reading every document. No backup format, data or rule changed
_changeNotes.PERF-0034: Listener and query bounds. Production Records re-subscribes only its production listener when the date filter changes (the date range is passed to the query; empty = the previous unbounded behaviour) while Master Data stays a mount-only fetch; Data Quality no longer fetches the full production history on open; the user list listener no longer re-subscribes on language change; system tests count documents instead of reading them. productionQueryBounds #17 failed only because its source window was too narrow after PERM-0027 added three fetches to the same mount-only effect - the effect was always mount-only; the window was widened and no application code changed for it
_changeNotes.DB-0033: Firestore rules for every collection this release writes, purely additive, deployed separately with firebase deploy --only firestore:rules. Master Data pattern (read signed-in, write admin): rotaryKilns, jobReferences, batches, boms, bomVersions, logicalItems, itemPairDecisions, routings, routingVersions, stages, costingPeriods, allocationSetups. Stage records (read/write signed-in, like the existing stage_* collections): stage_thermal_concrete, stage_tunnel_kiln, stage_handmade_brick. Import collections (read signed-in, create/update signed-in, delete admin): importSessions, importStagingRows, workOrders, stockScrap, workCenters. Corrected during release preparation: costingPeriods/allocationSetups had no rule (the Costing Setup panel could neither read nor save), and workCenters let any signed-in user delete a mapping the import never deletes. No existing rule was altered or weakened
_changeNotes.MOD-0032: Costing setup foundation (Phase 1 Step 8C). Costing periods (open/closed as a status, never deleted) and allocation setups are configured from Master Data by users who can import Master Data; writes are admin-only in the rules. Configuration only: nothing is calculated, allocated or posted, and no financial record is touched
_changeNotes.MOD-0031: Production traceability and new production areas (Phase 1 Steps 4 to 8C-5). Production references (job / batch / manufacturing order), actual consumption, production genealogy, quantity variance, unit readiness, record correction and packaging activity are attached by the existing entry forms and shown in Data Review. Three new stages - Thermal Concrete, Tunnel Kiln (team-based, continuous) and Hand-made Brick (pieces x piece weight) - each with its own stage_* collection, entry form and stage permission; a missing permission key falls back to the role preset, so existing users need no migration. Units are labels only: no Tons to Pieces conversion without an approved product-specific rule
_changeNotes.MOD-0030: Odoo three-file historical import (Phase 1 Step 8D). mrp.production, mrp.workorder and stock.scrap are read together, staged in importSessions/importStagingRows and reviewed before anything is written. Odoo ids stay external references; a production record is created only from a real production event (employee-only and continuation rows are participation, never production); repeated Chinese Mills rows across mills/shifts stay separate; stock.scrap is the only scrap source and is never subtracted from good production; Sorting and the Tunnel Kiln are team-based with no invented participation; السرد is never the rotary furnace and مركز الصب والفرم is never lightweight_foam; Work Center names stay distinct from Main Center identity; no fuzzy automatic merge; bad rows never block valid rows. Writing requires excel.import or historical.import.execute. No historical data was imported by this release
_changeNotes.MOD-0029: Entity Import engine and Master Data Package (Phase 1 Steps 8C-2 to 8E). One review flow - upload, parse, normalise, validate, preview, review, approval, user-triggered write - for jobs, batches, BOMs, routings, their versions, traced production and the reconciled Master Data package (products, materials, and each BOM with its single internal V1/DRAFT version, no invented effective dates, the Odoo BOM id kept as an external reference). Upserts by code then external reference, never by name; case-only duplicate codes keep the first record and SKIP the rest; CHR3600401F is a non-blocking warning; the six purchased raw materials and the two reject outputs are Ton; LCC-S9006 / LCC8004 / LCC-S8005 output Ton; units m2 and متر are approved with NO conversion to Ton or to each other; unsupported units are DEFERRED, never blocking. Writing requires excel.import and the Master Data rules (admin). Nothing was imported by this release
_changeNotes.MOD-0028: Master Data foundation (Phase 1 Steps 1A to 3, 7A). Item classification and overlap review, logical items, BOMs and BOM versions, routings and routing versions, the configurable Operation Master and its seed, equipment masters (tube/ball mills, bunkers, rotary kilns) grouped under one equipment category, job references and batches, external references, product-type seeding and Master Data quality checks, all through the existing audited Master Data service. Additive collections only; no existing record is migrated or rewritten
_changeNotes.PERM-0027: Production Records: canonical cost-centre filter and safe bulk delete. FILTER: the screen carried three controls for one organisational dimension - a multi-level drill-down with per-level checkbox columns, an equipment checklist beneath it (which said there was no equipment for a childless node), and a Code Type -> Codes pair. All three and their state are removed. The organisational filter is now the SAME CostCenterScopeSelector the Dashboard and Custom Dashboard use (search by code/name with path context, 5/6/7/8/9 groups, recursive checkboxes, clear, select all), over the canonical hierarchy index; ticked node ids go through the shared selection shape into the existing filterLegacyProductionRecords engine with the reconciled equipment links, so node -> descendants -> linked equipment -> records naming that press or furnace, and a leaf is its equipment. Date, cost centres, shift, product, a new customer filter (records already carry customerId) and search sit in one panel in the Dashboard filter-panel style with the export and new-entry actions. BULK DELETE (explicitly authorised): with production.delete (the existing key - no new permission) and at least one selected row, Delete Selected shows the exact count. The batch is selected ∩ visible, deduplicated, by document id, and is frozen when the confirmation opens; the confirmation states the deletion is permanent and cannot be undone through the current system. Nothing is deleted by selecting or by opening the dialog. On confirm, each record is checked against the live snapshot and passed to the existing deleteProductionRecord primitive one at a time - its existing audit entry per record, no batch write, no second delete service, no deleteStageRecord. Failures are isolated and nothing is rolled back; records already removed are skipped; a summary reports succeeded, failed (with ids), skipped and selected, and failed rows remain listed and selected for retry. No undo, restore or soft delete is claimed. Master Data, the hierarchy, Reports, AI and the Dashboard are not touched; no Firestore rule, schema or permission changed
_changeNotes.FIX-0026: Custom Dashboard filter and content integration. Two defects, both traced to their cause. (1) The widget grid was not stable: the Builder rendered `isLoading ? <loading box> : <sections>`, so every date change - which re-runs the shared, date-bounded fetch - unmounted the whole widget tree and rebuilt it, and unticking quantities (3.19.1) dropped it entirely, leaving an empty shell with the financial card as a separate area above. The sections container now always renders; loading, 'quantities not shown' and 'no data for this period / selection' are states inside each widget card, the financial value is a section of the same dashboard, and nothing uses a filter-derived key. Product, customer, shift, cost-centre and metric changes never refetched and still do not; widgets recompute from the one shared dataset through resolveWidgetFilters and the shared hierarchy scope. (2) A dashboard-wide Stage dropdown ('التشكيل والمكابس' once a saved or template dashboard set pressing) duplicated the organisational dimension the cost-centre hierarchy already provides. It is removed from the bar, and the dashboard filter state is normalised on EVERY write - the bar, a loaded, template or prefilled dashboard's saved defaults, the assistant's SET_FILTERS action, the AI designer, reset and save-as-default - so an old saved stage cannot linger as an invisible filter or be re-serialised. A widget keeps its own stage in its settings. The assistant's setCustomDashboardFilters no longer sends or reports a stage patch; a stage request is answered with where stage lives now. The classic Dashboard and Reports keep their own stage filters. One filter state, no new reads, no Firestore rule, schema, permission or data change
_changeNotes.UI-0025: Custom Dashboard visual parity with the classic Dashboard. Both already render in the same page container; the compression came from inside the Builder. Its Live Control Bar squeezed every filter into one overflow-x-auto strip of non-shrinking controls, which forced horizontal scrolling and clipped the cost-centre dropdown (an overflow container clips its absolutely positioned children), in a smaller light style unlike the classic dark filter panel; the dashboard name also appeared three times (a generic header, a narrow identity strip, and the filter bar). The filter panel now uses the classic Dashboard's own classes, extracted into shared dashboardFilterStyles tokens that the classic Dashboard uses too (identical class strings): period and actions, wrapping period presets, then a responsive 1/2/4-column filter grid with no scroll strip. The shared hierarchical cost-centre selector fills its cell and opens a 24rem panel capped at 90vw. The open dashboard is the page title with rename/duplicate/default/delete beside it and every dashboard action on the other side; section headers, widget toolbars and widget cards use the classic card treatment with readable controls; widget sizes and section columns are unchanged. The metric type toggle, financial card and gated financial read were moved out of DashboardView into shared DashboardMetricControls and reused by the Custom Dashboard, whose metric type is an optional field on the existing GlobalDashboardFilters (absent = QUANTITY, so saved dashboards are unchanged). No Firestore rule, schema, permission, query or data changed
_changeNotes.MOD-0024: Cost-centre selector search and recursive selection. The shared selector used by the classic Dashboard and the Custom Dashboard Builder gains a search box matching code, Arabic name and English name where present - case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant, and folding Arabic spelling variants through the existing normaliseLookupText rather than a new normaliser. Results keep hierarchy context: a matched child is shown under its ancestors and a matched parent with its branch, never as a flat list, and search changes only the rows shown, never the selection. Checkboxes are now recursive: checking a node selects it and its entire branch resolved from the FULL hierarchy (so a search cannot narrow what a tick selects), unchecking removes that branch and un-ticks its ancestors without touching any other branch, a partly selected branch shows its parents as indeterminate, and a parent becomes checked once all its children are. Select All adds every classified root, or every match while searching. All descendants, ancestors and children come from the shared hierarchy resolver over the already-loaded hierarchy; selection is local state with ids as identity, typing and ticking issue no Firestore read or write. The production and financial scopes read a materialised branch exactly as they read the parent alone, so Dashboard, Builder and Reports totals are unchanged for the same selection. No Firestore rule, schema, Report, AI, Production Records or production data changed
_changeNotes.DB-0023: Dashboard cost-centre unification and financial values. The classic Dashboard and the Custom Dashboard Builder each offered a flat legacy press/furnace list as the organisational filter; both now use ONE shared hierarchical cost-centre selector grouped under the existing 5/6/7/8/9 classifications, with multi-select checkboxes where a parent includes every descendant and a leaf is itself the target. What a selection covers is decided only by the shared resolver: for quantity it resolves node -> descendants -> linked equipment and is passed into the same filterUniversalRecords Reports uses, so Dashboard, Builder widgets, the Builder print view and its Excel export keep exactly the records Reports keeps for the same scope. An audit found no financial transaction storage anywhere, so the minimum model was added: a financialTransactions collection (date, accountCode, costCenterCode, amount, optional description/reference, importBatchId) with a dedicated Master Data importer beside Financial Accounts that never routes through Historical Import, validates the account and cost centre by exact code, and imports valid rows while keeping invalid rows on screen with their reason; writes go through the audited createMasterDataItem. The Dashboard gains a Metric Type selector (Quantities / Financial values): money is summed only from actual transactions, shown in its own card, never added to tonnage, and filtered only by date and cost centre - product, customer, shift and stage do not apply to it; transactions are read only when financial values are shown. Firestore rules gain a purely additive financialTransactions block (read signed-in, write admin, the financialAccounts pattern); it must be deployed separately before transactions can be read or imported. The reconciliation utility is kept because unresolved conflicts remain. No production record, legacy data, permission or Master Data category changed
_changeNotes.UI-0022: Master Data unification. The screen carried THREE category controls at once - a dropdown, a multi-select panel and a category row - and the dropdown opened the hierarchy maintenance modal when cost centres were chosen, so browsing cost-centre master data was not reachable at all. Two of the three are removed; one row is the whole navigation. Presses, furnaces, mills and the legacy departments list are no longer primary categories: they are the same business entities the imported hierarchy already represents, and listing them again showed one machine as two master records. Their collections are untouched and still reached through the equipment -> hierarchyNodeId link that Production Records, Reports and the assistant use. Cost Centers now serve the imported hierarchy itself, registered as a normal tab so the SAME cache-first read and live subscription serve it, with the 5/6/7/8/9 classifications inline on the same screen and never in a modal. The generic column-mapped importer is excluded from the hierarchy at the type level, since it has its own Sheet1 importer. No data deleted, no production record touched, no Firestore rule, schema or permission changed
_changeNotes.UI-0021: Master Data three-panel organisation. Area 1 is a multi-select code-type picker with checkboxes over the seven registry categories; Area 2 shows exactly the selected ones and switches which is active; Area 3 shows only the active category's data, with an explicit empty state instead of a stale table. Unticking the active category moves focus rather than leaving Area 3 pointing at something no longer listed, and a category that is not selected can never become active. Cost Centres gain 5/6/7/8/9 sub-category filtering that REUSES the existing Sheet1 root-category rule (ROOT_CATEGORY_CODES/ROOT_CATEGORY_LABELS, root = the code's first character) rather than restating it - a code like 0501 is therefore reported as unclassified rather than forced into 5, since the leading zero is significant. The sub-filter is one more AND over the existing search, status and prefix filters. activeTab remains the engine, so the table, Add/Edit modal, importers, export, per-row actions, permissions and audit are untouched; the Cost Center Hierarchy browser and the reconciliation utility stay separate utilities, not categories
_changeNotes.MOD-0020: Enable Apply Safe Matches. The panel action, disabled in 3.15.1 while the UI was being verified, now writes the validated plan through the applier service that has been in place and tested since 3.15.0. The button applies exactly `plannedLinks` - the plan the panel is displaying - so the confirmed count is the written count, and nothing is re-matched at write time: conflicts and no-counterpart rows never enter the plan, so they cannot be written. One field, hierarchyNodeId, on one legacy equipment record, through the audited updateMasterDataItem. Failures isolate with no rollback; a row already pointing at the planned node is skipped, so a second run writes nothing. After a successful apply the equipment list is re-read with skipCache so the panel recomputes and the applied rows stop showing as pending. No production document, Firestore rule, schema, permission, Report or AI code changed
_changeNotes.FIX-0019: Make the reconciliation reachable. The panel shipped in 3.14/3.15 was an inline banner gated on being on an equipment tab AND having a non-zero matched or ambiguous count, so with the hierarchy not yet imported both counts were zero and it rendered on no tab at all - the feature existed in the bundle and nowhere on screen. It is now a dedicated Master Data utility, "Reconcile Codes with Hierarchy", beside the existing quality-report actions, opening a panel that always shows all four buckets including zeroes and an explicit no-data state. Reconciliation now spans presses, furnaces and mills together instead of only the open tab. Read-only by design for this step: the applier service is not imported by the screen at all and the Apply button is rendered disabled, so opening the panel cannot write. The Cost Center Hierarchy browser is a separate control and is untouched
_changeNotes.MOD-0018: Persist the safe legacy-to-hierarchy links. A new CONFLICT outcome was added first, because the 3.14.0 plan would have overwritten a record already linked to a DIFFERENT node - harmless while nothing was written, a silent reassignment once it is. Conflicts now never reach `matched`, so they cannot reach the plan: the protection is structural rather than a filter. The applier consumes the already-validated plan without re-matching, writes one field on one legacy record through the existing audited updateMasterDataItem (permissions, validation, audit and cache invalidation inherited), isolates every failure so 97 successes survive 3 errors with no rollback, and skips a row already pointing at the planned node so a second run writes nothing. Master Data gains an Apply Safe Matches action with an explicit confirmation naming the exact count and stating that historical records are untouched. Ambiguous, conflicting and unmatched rows stay visible for manual review. No production document, Firestore rule, schema or permission changed
_changeNotes.MOD-0017: Legacy code reconciliation and true multi-select hierarchy. A new pure engine matches legacy equipment records to imported hierarchy nodes by exact business code WITHIN the same category, returning MATCHED / AMBIGUOUS / UNMATCHED; names are carried into the report but never compared, so differing names for the same code reconcile and a shared code across categories never does. Only an unambiguous one-to-one match is safe to persist, and the release writes nothing - Master Data shows the dry run. The derived link also completes equipment links in memory so a hierarchy leaf resolves to its legacy equipment immediately, which is what ends the false "no equipment" on a childless node: having no children is no longer treated as having no equipment. The selector became multi-select at EVERY level - each level is the deduplicated union of the children of what is ticked above it, a deeper tick narrows (so parent plus child cannot double-count), unticking a parent cascades its descendants away, and select-all covers only the nodes visible at that level. Reports, AI and the Dashboard inherit the corrected links through the one shared resolver
_changeNotes.MOD-0016: Hierarchical production filter UI. Production Records gains a multi-level production-centre drill-down: level 1 is the hierarchy's real roots, each later level is exactly the chosen node's children, depth is whatever the data has, and equipment is ticked with checkboxes at the current branch. Stopping at any level means the whole branch below it; ticking narrows to exactly what is ticked and can never widen. Navigation discards deeper levels and ticks from the branch being left, so a stale selection cannot leak across branches. The Dashboard equipment selector now follows the selected stage instead of always listing presses - options come from a registry declaration of which equipment each stage actually records, read off the entry forms: only pressing writes pressId/furnaceId, so every other stage now says it has no equipment rather than offering a filter that could only ever match nothing; an incompatible selection is cleared when the stage changes. Both screens resolve through the one shared resolver and agree on the same equipment ids. filterUniversalRecords gained an additive furnaceId clause that Reports never set
_changeNotes.AI-0015: AI hierarchy integration. A new deterministic lookup service (hierarchyNodeLookupPure) resolves production-centre text to a hierarchy node by exact code, then exact canonical name, then exact localized name, returning FOUND / AMBIGUOUS / NOT_FOUND. Ambiguous names ask which branch was meant using real paths; unknown names say so rather than answering zero; fuzzy matching is offered only as a did-you-mean suggestion and never resolves. The EXISTING generateReport tool gained one optional productionCenters field and routes the resolved node ids through the same shared equipment resolver and the same filterUniversalRecords the Reports screen uses, so assistant totals equal report totals by construction rather than by coincidence. No provider, no Global AI Chat, no aggregation formula, no permission, no Firestore rule and no production record changed; the legacy productionQueryTools path is deliberately left out because it aggregates differently
_changeNotes.UI-0014: Hierarchy-aware reporting. The Reports screen gains a production-centre scope selector: choosing a node scopes the report to that node plus every descendant node's linked equipment, resolved once through the shared resolver and deduplicated before any record is examined, so overlapping branches never double-count. A stage record's equipment is read from rawData (pressId/furnaceId/machineId/equipmentId), ALL of them rather than the first, so a record naming both a press and a furnace belongs to both branches yet is still counted once. The scope is an additional AND beside date, stage, product, customer, employee and shift; with no selection the filtering is the identity case and every report is byte-identical to before. Aggregation formulas, exports and permissions are untouched - export already flows from the same filtered dataset. Records from the seven stages that carry no equipment reference are excluded from a press/furnace scope rather than silently kept, because membership must be provable. No AI, Firestore rule, schema or production document changed
_changeNotes.MOD-0013: Equipment -> hierarchy link. Press, Furnace and Mill master records gain a persisted, nullable hierarchyNodeId holding a stable hierarchy node id. A production record is now resolved to the hierarchy as record -> pressId/furnaceId -> equipment master record -> hierarchyNodeId -> ancestors, so selecting a parent node includes every descendant node's linked equipment WITHOUT modifying a single historical production document and with no migration. The shared hierarchy resolver gained the equipment layer (buildEquipmentByNode, resolveEquipmentForHierarchyNode(s), validateEquipmentLink); there is still exactly one descendant walk. Master Data gains a node selector on the equipment tabs, a link-status column and an unlinked-count banner. Assignment is explicit: no fuzzy matching is used as the authoritative relationship. Financial Accounts and Cost Centers remain Master-Data-only. No Firestore rule changed - presses/furnaces already allowed admin writes
_changeNotes.UI-0012: Production Records code filter: the press-only selector is replaced by a category then code filter driven by the shared Master Data registry. Adds furnace, customer and shift as filter dimensions and multi-code selection, with an empty code list meaning ALL so that mode never materialises the code list. The registry gained a separate legacyProductionFields declaration because the `production` collection is a different record shape from UniversalStageRecord - it has no stageType but does carry pressId, furnaceId and shiftId. Financial Accounts and Cost Centers remain Master-Data-only: no production record field links to them. The hierarchy expansion is shared with the stage-record resolver but no legacy category is hierarchical, because nothing links a production record to a hierarchy node
_changeNotes.MOD-0011: Row-selection foundation for the Production Records table: per-row and header checkboxes in a dedicated column, a visible/selected counter, select-all-visible and deselect-all controls, and pruning of stale selections on filter change. Reuses the existing bulkEditPure selection primitives rather than adding a second selection architecture. Selection is UI state only - no Firestore read or write - and no bulk action of any kind is attached to it; in particular no bulk delete
_changeNotes.UI-0010: Financial Accounts import opens a dedicated Master Data importer instead of the Historical Excel Import screen: the action no longer navigates to the bulk-entry route (which App.tsx renders as DataImportView); a new in-place modal reuses the existing financialAccounts schema, XLSX reader, row validation, duplicate detection and chunked commit, adds sheet selection and parent/cycle relationship checks, and keeps partial import so invalid rows never block valid ones
_changeNotes.DB-0009: Category-first Master Data over an extensible registry; Financial Accounts master data with Excel import and hierarchical editing (new financialAccounts collection and its Firestore rule); one shared generic hierarchy resolver reused by Master Data, Production Review and production aggregation; hierarchical cost-centre editing with cycle, self-parent and unknown-parent protection
